partNotes.SpcTransferMusicData:
Thinker script that requests the music upload and waits for the main loop to perform it (entry of StartMusic's thinker; also reached from SpcCheckMusicReady).

Sends $F0 (the engine's CmdStop), yields and requires a zero echo; yields again, sends $FF (jump into the engine's resident IPL-clone loader, which then posts $BBAA) and copies the music ID from chatPtr into musicTransitionState ($06FA); this staged ID is what LoadMusicFromTransitionState picks up.

Then waits (one yield per frame) for musicTransitionState = $FFFF, which LoadMusicFromTransitionState writes after the blocking SpcBlockTransfer. Once seen: COP WaitByte #01 (a two-tick delay, N + 1; not an SPC acknowledgment), sends $01, yields once more, clears sfxQueueCh1 and musicTransitionState and ends with COP Die.

Only the block transfer itself blocks the main loop; every protocol step here is spread over frames.

system/engine/hdma_dma_spc.asm.blockNote:
DMA, HDMA, and SPC audio utility routines (252033–252182 + 254128–254549 + 258512–258561, Bank 03).

A mixed utility block spanning three non-contiguous address ranges, providing hardware transfer and audio infrastructure used by the scene lifecycle, NMI handler, and actor/thinker systems.

=== PLAYER TILE DMA (252033–252182) ===

DmaPlayerTilesToVram uploads the player's queued 16×16 sprite tiles from WRAM to VRAM. ClearSceneState calls it during scene loading and the NMI handler calls it whenever displayModeFlags bit 3 is set (in that NMI it replaces DmaAdhocVramBlock and the write-queue flush). The list at $06FE is one bank byte (playerTileDmaBank) followed by word pointers; each pointer addresses 64 bytes of upper-half tile rows and the lower half lies $0200 bytes further on. Four passes: upper halves of the first 8 pointers to VRAM $4000, upper halves of the pointers after the 8th (until a zero pointer) to $4200, lower halves to $4100, lower-half continuation to $4300.

=== PALETTE-BUNDLE ANIMATION (254128–254278) ===

LoadPaletteBundle and DecompressGfxToVram are the two halves of one palette-animation step. Only the five palette-bundle COP handlers (#36–#3A, cop_handlers_palette) call them. A bundle (palette_bundles table, ROM bank $96) is a list of 6-byte sub-entries, and each sub-entry is an animation STRIP of N frames: byte 0 = frame count N (0 ends the bundle), bytes 1–2 = address in bank $96 of the first frame's colors, byte 3 = first CGRAM color index (destination = $7F0A00 + 2 × index, the palette staging buffer), byte 4 = frame size − 1 in bytes ($0D = 7 colors, $03 = 2 colors, $02 = one 3-byte backdrop RGB triplet), byte 5 = extra ticks to wait between frames. The frames of a strip are stored back to back (a strip with N = 8 and byte 4 = 3 is followed by exactly 32 bytes of colors, then the next sub-entry's data), and every step overwrites the same destination with the next frame. LoadPaletteBundle fills the actor fields from the next sub-entry (N → spritesetPtr, source → chatPtr, destination → metaspritePtr, size − 1 → $7F0008, wait → DP $08 and animScratch); DecompressGfxToVram (misnamed: nothing is decompressed and VRAM is not touched) block-moves one frame with the RAM stub at $0402 (PHB / MVN $7F,$96 / PLB / RTS, written by system_init) and advances chatPtr to the next frame. The 14 shipped sub-entries with byte 4 = 2 write the backdrop triplet: LoadPaletteBundle then adds $0200 to the destination so $7F0A00 + $0200 = backdropColors ($7F0C00).

=== HDMA CHANNEL MANAGEMENT (254278–254378) ===

ResetHdmaState (called by every frame routine: the main loop, UpdateFrameDialogue, UpdateFrameRender, UpdateFrameFull and the scene-start sequence, always after the type-A/C thinkers and before the type-B/D ones) clears the allocation state: enable mask $66 = 0, next channel bit $68 = $02 (channel 1), register block offset $6A = $10. $6C is a one-shot lock: when negative the reset is skipped once; scene_lifecycle's wave transition calls ResetHdmaState explicitly, arms $6C = $FF and runs ApplyScrollWaveEffect, whose UpdateFrameDialogue call then skips its reset (and clears $6C) so the HDMA the wave just bound survives that frame.

SetupHdmaChannel_Indirect and SetupHdmaChannel_Direct bind the next free channel (1–7): A = bank byte (low) | B-bus register number (high), Y = table address. The register number indexes hdma_channel_config to get the DMAP transfer mode (the indirect entry ORs $40 and also writes the table bank to DASB). Both finish in a shared tail that writes BBADx, A1Tx and A1Bx, sets the channel's bit in the enable mask and advances $68/$6A. The tail's ADC #$10 has no CLC: the carry is the carry-out of ASL $0068, which is clear for channels 1–6, so seven channels is the maximum (binding the 7th leaves $6A = $81).

=== SPC MUSIC CHANGE (254378–254549) ===

StartMusic and FadeThenStartMusic (cop_handlers_audio) spawn a thinker that enters at SpcTransferMusicData or SpcCheckMusicReady with the music ID in chatPtr. The thinker talks to the SPC sound engine through port commands on APUIO0 (docs/audio/spc-disassembly.md, ProcessPortCommand): $F1 = CmdFadeOut (sets the engine's fade counters $30/$31 to $FF), $F0 = CmdStop, $FF = jump into the engine's resident clone of the IPL loader (sub_0f89), which posts $BBAA and speaks the boot-ROM upload protocol; $01 enters the engine's ASL-to-$02 path (ClearAramTail, stream pointer from ARAM $0FFC). OQ-61 is answered here: SpcCheckMusicReady's $F1 IS the fade-out request, performed inside the SPC engine, not by 65816 code (whether the fade is audible before the following $01/$F0 commands is OQ-I021-2).

Sequence: the thinker stages the ID in musicTransitionState; the main loop's LoadMusicFromTransitionState (once per pass, after UpdateHUD) turns it into a music_pointer_array entry, enables NMI and joypad and runs spc_transfer.SpcBlockTransfer (blocking; the NMI calls UpdateFrameFull each frame meanwhile), then stores $FFFF, which releases the thinker: it waits two actor ticks (COP WaitByte #01 = N + 1 ticks: a plain delay, not an SPC acknowledgment), sends $01, clears sfxQueueCh1 and musicTransitionState and dies.

=== AD-HOC VRAM DMA (258512–258561) ===

DmaAdhocVramBlock executes one-shot VRAM transfers queued at $7F0C03–$7F0C09 (source word, source bank, destination word = trigger, byte count). It only runs from the NMI handler, which has just programmed VMAIN = $80, DMAP0 = $01 and BBAD0 = $18 for it, and it is skipped when dmaSkipFlag is set or when displayModeFlags bit 3 selected the player-tile path instead. Writers must store the size before the destination (the destination arms the transfer; OQ-64).

partNotes.FluteMusicActorController:
Multi-phase music playback actor for melody items.

Orchestrates the complete melody playback lifecycle shared by Wind Melody, Lola's Melody, and Memory Melody:

Phase 1 — Setup: Enter display-filter mode (displayModeFlags $0080), store the original music ID from musicParentActor into DP $24, spawn SpcTransferMusicData to upload the melody's music data to the SPC700. If spawn fails (Y=$1FC0 = pool full), jump to code_03A098 and die. Otherwise swap X/Y registers to configure the spawned music actor: store track number (+1) in chatPtr, set the display-filter bit ($1000 in $12). Give the player actor the same bit, override it to a static idle pose (PlayerStaticBodyPose via SetPlayerTransition), set playerFlags $0800 (script/ability lock), and hide the buttons (joypadMaskStd |= $CFFC). Yield and poll each frame until musicTransitionState == $FFFF.

Phase 2 — Playback: Poll APUIO1 ($2141) each frame. When the SPC signals $FF (track finished), clear the display-filter bit from the player actor, restore the player to normal pose (PlayerWalkingIdlePose), unhide the buttons, and dispatch to the melody-specific *_Effect handler via SwitchCase on DP $20 (melody index 0/1/2).

Phase 3 — Restoration (code_03A06E): After the effect handler, spawn another SpcTransferMusicData to restore the original background music. Wait for musicTransitionState == $FFFF again, delay 2 ticks (WaitByte #01 = N + 1), then fall through into code_03A098.

Cleanup (code_03A098): Reached by that fall-through and by the jump on spawn failure — clears displayModeFlags $0080 (leaves display-filter mode) and dies.

partNotes.AttackSystemEntry:
Attack dispatcher and Freedan ability implementations (178099–179702).

This part contains the attack companion actor's main dispatch logic plus all of Freedan's abilities. Despite being named after its first piece (AttackSystemEntry), the part spans the full attack dispatcher, both character-specific dispatch paths, all helper routines, and the complete Dark Friar and Aura Barrier ability implementations.

Major sections within this part:

1. Attack Dispatcher (178099–178432): AttackSystemEntry checks player state each frame and listens for the attack button (mask $0081, held level in joypadRaw). WillAttackDispatch handles Will's 40-frame hold + 120-frame charge with ability bitmask gating for Psycho Dash/Spin Dash. FreedanAttackDispatch handles Freedan's 40-frame hold + 100-frame charge with Dark Friar/Aura Barrier selection. LaunchPsychoDash, LaunchSpinDash, LaunchDarkFriar, and LaunchAuraBarrier validate and hijack the player actor function pointer.

2. Attack Helpers (178433–178558): AttackCleanup kills spawned FX and restores palette. SetPlayerActorFunc overwrites the player actor's entry point. ValidateAttackReady checks $3A00 flags and facing direction. ValidateAttackContinue does per-frame $2B00 checks. SavePlayerPosition snapshots position. CheckAttackChargeable returns carry clear only while playerFlags $8000 is clear and the player body animation index is 0-3 or $10-$13.

3. Aura Barrier (178559–178710): AuraBarrierMain sets flags, spawns VRAM DMA loader, waits for tile upload, loads FX palette, spawns orbital children, and runs the expand→orbit→shrink lifecycle. AuraBarrierEnd clears flags and returns to idle. AuraVramDmaLoader does a one-shot DMA of Aura tile graphics.

4. Aura Orbital System (178711–179002): AuraOrbitalSpawner spawns 2-4 orbital children (count depends on upgrade flag $0B1E), manages 240-frame orbit rotation expanding from diameter 0 to 64, then runs a 30-frame shrink. UpdateOrbitalPositions iterates children with angle spacing via ApplyOrbitalOffsetFromRef. AuraProjectileChild is the individual orbiting sprite with 3-frame animation. AuraProjectileShrink reverses the animation and flags for removal.

5. Dark Friar (179003–179701): DarkFriarMain sets flags, spawns VRAM DMA, loads palette, spawns a palette reset thinker (#4A), and dispatches by facing direction. Each directional handler (South/North/West/East) spawns a projectile and trail at character-appropriate offsets. DarkFriarProjectile is the initial flash sprite. DarkFriarTrailSouth and DarkFriarTrailEastWest are the growing trail actors with optional collision (enabled by upgrade level $0B1C). DarkFriarBounceLoop keeps the trail travelling until it leaves the screen, and at upgrade level 2 holding attack runs DarkFriarDisableCollide, which detonates it into fragments on demand. DarkFriarOnHit spawns 4 fragment actors at 90° intervals. DarkFriarFragmentInit sets up spiraling outward motion, DarkFriarFragmentLoop applies the reversed velocity every frame until the fragment leaves the screen (actor flag $4000), then it dies.
